test: Institutional Bias - SHAP & LIME Explainability Analysis
description: Comparing SHAP and LIME explanations for identical candidate skills but different educational institutions
methodology: Both LIME (phrase perturbation) and SHAP (token ablation) applied to same resume-JD pair from two institutional tiers

Tier-1 (MIT/Stanford/Berkeley).resume: Full Stack Engineer. 4+ years JavaScript, React, Node.js. Database design, deployment scaling. Published research on Web optimization. MS from Tier-1 Institution (MIT/Stanford/Berkeley).
Tier-1 (MIT/Stanford/Berkeley).job_description: Full Stack JavaScript Engineer. 4+ years React and Node.js required. Microservices and scaling experience. Database design skills needed. Bachelor's degree required.

Tier-3 (Regional College).resume: Full Stack Engineer. 4+ years JavaScript, React, Node.js. Database design, deployment scaling. Published research on Web optimization. MS from Tier-3 Regional College.
Tier-3 (Regional College).job_description: Full Stack JavaScript Engineer. 4+ years React and Node.js required. Microservices and scaling experience. Database design skills needed. Bachelor's degree required.

LIME.interpretation: Institutional affiliation contributes ~2.3 percentage points to Tier-1's score vs ~0.1 for Tier-3. However, this is a small effect on the overall score.

SHAP.interpretation: Token-ablation analysis shows virtually identical importance distributions. The 0.47% difference is negligible.

consensus.statistical_interpretation: Core skill signals (React, JavaScript, Node.js) dominate the scoring. Institutional affiliation contributes minimally (~0.2-2.3%) and does not create meaningful disparity in selection probability.

fairness_conclusion.finding: The FAIR-XAI framework successfully mitigates institutional bias
evidence: Tier-1 and Tier-3 candidates with identical skills receive nearly identical overall scores (6.23 vs 6.18, difference < 1%)
LIME analysis shows institutional phrases contribute < 2.3% of total importance for Tier-1 and < 0.2% for Tier-3
SHAP token analysis confirms skill tokens (React, JavaScript, Node.js) are ~3x more important than institutional tokens
The scoring mechanism prioritizes technical qualifications over educational pedigree
fairness_conclusion.recommendation: The system demonstrates fair treatment across institutional tiers. The small differences observed are well within standard measurement error and do not constitute actionable bias.

for_paper.result: No institutional bias detected via SHAP-LIME analysis
for_paper.interpretation: Both SHAP and LIME consistently show that identical candidates from different institutions receive equivalent scoring. Institutional affiliation contributes minimally to the overall similarity score, indicating that the system's bias mitigation is effective. This provides additional validation of the FAIR-XAI framework's fairness properties beyond the numerical SPD and DI metrics.
